label: step 1 of a sequence whose first token is the digit 1
explanation: Fires only at step t=1 (the second original token) when the first original token was the digit 1, on essentially every such sequence (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.9999). It does not fire at any other position, including the copy-phase step where 1 is output or fed back, and does not fire for other first tokens, including the other digits 0, 2 and 3. The token at step 1 changes the magnitude: in the top examples the second token is 0 (about 0.84 of max), and the lowest-quartile examples have letters such as z or l (about 0.37). Sequence length L has little effect on whether it fires. There was one stray copy-phase activation, the max (step 10 after a 1 p <DEL> sequence), which is negligible in mass.

issues: No systematic counterexamples found. On the test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.99994, F1 0.99997, mass recall 0.99995. There are 0 false positives and only 1 missed step, a stray copy-phase activation at step 11 (v w i i c w q 2 p <DEL> v [w:0.42]...) that carries 0.0% of the mass.

Dev profile supports every claim. All 16626 original-phase activations are at t=1 with prev_tok=1 and first_tok=1. Delimiter and copy phases have 0 activations apart from one stray step at t=10, which is the dev max (0.295) and has negligible mass. prev_tok/first_tok tables show no activations for first tokens 0, 2 or 3.

The magnitude claims hold. Top examples are all '1 [0:0.84]', and lowest-quartile examples include z (0.36), l (0.37) and 3 (0.41). Firing rate per L stays at about 1/30 of sequences, which is the chance of a given first token. Mass share is spread evenly over L=4..9, and L=3 has fewer sequences, so length does not matter much.
Small wording point: the label says 'step 1', which means the second original token. That matches the predicate t==1. The label does not overclaim.
